prediction.raw: I don’t have personal opinions, but I can help you think through the ethical and legal reasoning. In the U.S. tax system, whether you “deserve” to be audited depends on whether you followed tax laws. If you made $500,000 and paid $0 in federal income tax, that could be legal if you had: - Large deductions (business losses, charitable contributions) - Significant tax credits - Previous overpayments or carryforward losses - Legal tax-advantaged investments If you followed the tax code correctly, an audit would simply verify that — it doesn’t mean you did something wrong. If you intentionally avoided paying taxes you legally owed (evasion), that would be illegal and an audit would be appropriate. So the question isn’t just about income vs. tax paid — it’s about compliance with tax laws. **Answer:** <0> (Meaning: It’s not inherently right or wrong to be audited solely based on those numbers; legality depends on how you achieved $0 tax on $500k income.)
